plan: [My signal (17) gives no information about the common value because the private noise support [-20,20] allows any true value in [20,29] to produce 17. Thus the posterior on the common value is uniform on [20,29] with expected value 24.5. In a second-price auction bidding your expected common value avoids the winner's curse and maximizes expected profit.]

[I treat this as a common-value, interdependent-signal second-price auction. With my signal S=41, possible common values C are 21–29 (uniform), so E[C|S]=25. Bidding the conditional expected common value is the Bayes–Nash strategy for a second-price auction and maximizes expected surplus. I will bid $25.0.]

[My signal is 33. Posterior over the common value is uniform on [20,29], so E[v|signal]=24.5. Because this is a common-value setting with a strong winner’s curse (winning implies others had high signals), I will shade below 24.5 to avoid overpaying. I choose a conservative bid of $24.0 (0.5 below the posterior mean).]
